subject: P0 usability failure: Four Locks UX/art recovery; integrated acceptance required
body:
# Orchard player experience recovery:2 October2026

Priority: P0, ahead of further banks, new families or optional art. Sam tried the integrated slice and could not understand the mission/actions; the earlier illustrated appearance has regressed. QA-01 is FAILED for current player experience. Prior route/reducer tests remain useful engineering evidence but are not playable acceptance. No more requests for Sam to play the current version as a finished preview.

## Verified cause

Primary route in ExpeditionScreen.jsx bypasses its existing illustrated setup. OrchardExpedition Setup uses selects/fieldsets and a flat CSS surface. MapViewport renders terrain as coloured SVG polygons and a gradient backdrop. orchardArtFor resolves heroes, enemies and orchard but no scenic terrain/background/chrome. Existing legacy assets and presentation source remain present: expedition-9fo-scene-art.js, expedition-9fo-art.js, expedition-9fo-extra-art.js, wm-9fo-ui-art.js, runtime/backgrounds/po-orchard-gorge-v1.webp and runtime terrain/UI kit. Do not delete or replace these unnecessarily. Asset presence/import counts do not prove actual integration.

Briefing compresses puzzle, circuits, three jobs, charge, enemy phases and alternate alcove into paragraphs. Setup says solve ledger/choose circuits/hold without teaching those terms. AbilityHand currently offers names/cost/readiness without purpose. Base buttons expose engine command names; object drawer mostly offers position and generic rail instruction. This is an experience defect, not a player failure.

## Ownership and scope

Codex owns v2 UI/art recovery. Claude owns engine, App route/progress and final shared build. No overlap or engine numerical changes; preserve exact private gate, printed-stat requirements, AP rules and3-star first-clear awards. Reuse legacy visual assets in Codex v2 components using selected metadata/imports; do not edit legacy/shared renderer or registries without explicit transfer. Avoid wholesale registry imports where they bloat the bundle. No new scenes/heroes/enemy factions. Read art pipeline and preflight before new selected derivatives. Engine-provided previews/results remain authority.

## First delivery: coherent Four Locks player flow

1. Illustrated mission/squad selection: restore the Orchard backdrop, briefing panel, three portrait-based team slots, card selection highlights and familiar framed controls. Show one available mission and difficulty clearly; unavailable families belong in a secondary future-content view, not five prominent disabled choices. Owned cards only. Explain each job by its task before its mathematical name; show the relevant printed-stat requirement beside candidate cards. Preserve warned attempts and alcove alternative; never silently alter the squad. No unexplained dropdown wall.
2. Map appearance: reuse accepted grass/path/roots/water/hedge/bridge tiles, scenic backdrop, station props and HUD/hero/action frames. Logical exact pointy geometry, hit polygons and overlays remain code. Measured top/ground anchors and uniform scale prevent old art distortion. State cues must show blocked/open paths, threats, charged stations and holders clearly. Labels must remain readable and the board dominant at desktop/tablet/phone sizes. Missing art may use a documented restrained interim only for genuinely unsupported states.
3. Opening explanation, maximum three short stages with map highlights: the orchard is in danger; solve its number lock to activate two helpful mechanisms; fill and staff the three marked stations together; survive the enemy turn before the deadline. Every claim matches production blueprint/rules. Connect each station to its map marker and show a checklist updating from real state. Explain round/action points before the first move: each hero has two actions; enemies act when End round is confirmed. Distinguish free puzzle editing from the paid activation action.
4. Guided first actions, opt-in and reopenable: select a hero, highlight legal movement, preview a move, confirm it, show the changed location/AP. Then guide opening/solving the number lock and explain selected circuit effects with labelled before/after map changes. Progress triggers follow accepted engine events, not a guessed fixed solution or coordinate. Do not prescribe every tactical choice, provide a free win, modify pressure or turn the tutorial into a new small/easier game. Allow skip/reopen; resuming a run must not replay blocking onboarding.
5. Plain-language glossary at point of use: a circuit is one chosen mechanism effect; charge is a station's stored power; Hold means stay working there through the enemy turn; activation applies the solved draft to the board. Replace abstract commission terminology in main objective with the actual success condition. Keep technical identities internal where possible. Show concrete object names and map highlight rather than axial coordinates in the main flow; text/keyboard board remains available.
6. Contextual actions: hero selection shows a compact relevant set; tapping a station/enemy shows what this hero can do there and why other useful actions are unavailable. Each base action and every ability card includes a one-sentence purpose, cost, range/target and governing printed stat. Expand exact calculation in preview. Retain all legal moves, including wait/refocus/repair/protect/alcove, in an accessible expanded action list; contextual hiding must not remove tactical options. Disabled reasons explain how to make an action possible.
7. Action/result feedback: preview clearly says who, what target, cost, expected change and any downside; Confirm executes once. Result shows the same change near the affected object and in a readable message. Combat example format: governing stat + support/bonuses - armour = damage, enemy health before/after, survives/defeated. Use production factors, never duplicate engine calculations. Protection and repair explain duration and protected target. Stations show power/capacity and readiness; hold cancellation explains its cause.
8. Enemy turn: highlight enemy, target and intention on map before confirming End round; afterwards explain actual movement/damage/disruption and orchard loss in a short ordered recap. The player must see why damage happened and the next useful response. Never leave this only in a full log drawer.
9. Result/retry: explain actual success or failure conditions, first-clear versus replay reward, and a concrete next-attempt hint. No generic expedition ended message without cause.

## Delivery sequence and gates

A. Inspect actual integrated route and capture baseline screenshots. Publish reused assets and proposed restored setup/board/first-turn layout in owner report. Then implement this Four Locks recovery in Codex-owned components; validate via the real controller route. If a needed change is Claude-owned, send exact interface requirement in mailbox and continue independent work.
B. Produce actual browser screenshots of setup, briefing, movement preview/result, puzzle activation, station actions, ability explanation, enemy preview/recap and result. Target desktop, tablet and narrow phone. Source inspection, server-rendered/static mockups and jsdom are supplemental, not browser visual evidence. Record actual environment; if browser unavailable report it, do not claim acceptance.
C. Complete one reference win through UI controls and a failed attempt, checking save/resume, first reward and zero replay reward. Retain real winning trace, no UI state injection to claim interactive success. Claude supplies integration fixes/full build under final-build lock as necessary. Tests should cover meaningful learning/action flows and preview/result consistency, not copy text snapshots alone.
D. Scrum visually reviews against old assets/mockups and verifies that goal, next action, cost and enemy result are understandable without reading design docs. Only then invite Sam for a short usability review. QA-01 stays failed/pending until evidence addresses his actual complaint. Device/child timing remain unavailable until separately tested.

Do not prioritise more art generation over applying the large existing kit. Keep the agreed tactical depth; clarity comes from staging explanations and linking them to the board. Overnight automation remains paused; this is a new daytime recovery priority authorised by Sam's feedback.
